name: The Nature of Actual Sin

objectives.text: Identify sin as disobeying what God says in his Word
Give examples of sin in thoughts, words, and actions from everyday life
Recite the catechism definition of sin and explain in their own words what it means to fall short of God's law and to break it
Distinguish sins of commission from sins of omission using examples from Scripture and daily life
Compare outward sinful acts with the sinful desires and thoughts of the heart from which Jesus says they come
Explain how the tenth commandment shows that God's law forbids sinful desire as well as sinful deeds
Trace the progression from temptation to sinful desire to sinful act described in James
Analyze why breaking one commandment makes a person a lawbreaker of the whole law as given by one Lawgiver
Interpret Jesus' teaching on anger and lust in the Sermon on the Mount to show that God's law reaches the inner person
Explain from the Mosaic law and the Psalms why unintentional sins and sins done in ignorance are still sins before God
Explain from the examples of Joseph and David why all sin is ultimately committed against God himself
Distinguish actual sins from original sin as the Reformed confessions describe actual transgressions proceeding from a corrupt nature
Analyze the main Hebrew and Greek words for sin, such as missing the mark, rebellion, iniquity, transgression, and lawlessness, and what each reveals about its nature
Construct a biblical taxonomy of actual sin that organizes sins by thought, word, and deed and by commission and omission with supporting texts
Analyze how Scripture presents sin at root as a failure to love God and neighbor and as exchanging the worship of God for created things
Evaluate contemporary definitions of wrongdoing, such as harm to others or personal mistakes, against the biblical definition of sin as offense against God's law
Synthesize Paul's teaching that the law functions as a mirror that makes sin known and explain how the Reformed tradition describes this use of the law

changes: Merged the K and grade 1 objectives on sin as disobedience into one. Replaced the grade 2 recall about everyone sinning (universality belongs to The Extent and Gravity of Sin) with examples of sin in thought, word, and deed, and folded the grade 3 observation into it. Kept and reworded the WSC Q14 definition, commission and omission, heart versus outward acts, the tenth commandment, James 2:10, the Sermon on the Mount (now anchored to WLC Q99), sin against God, the taxonomy, and the law as mirror (with WLC Q95). Reframed the corrupt nature objective as distinguishing actual from original sin with WCF 6.4 and WSC Q18. Dropped the two grade 11 objectives on small sins and the seriousness of sin as they belong to The Extent and Gravity of Sin. Added objectives on the James 1 progression from temptation to sin, unintentional sins, the biblical vocabulary of sin, sin as failure of love and idolatry, and evaluating cultural definitions of wrongdoing. Removed Romans 6:23, Habakkuk 1:13, and WLC Q152 as they concern consequences and gravity.
